result.rationale: The diff shows `ensure_embeddable` raises Discourse::InvalidAccess when `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`; a missing Referer yields an empty host that never matches, so all no-Referer visitors (privacy extensions, proxies, referrer-suppressing policies) are hard-blocked with a 403 inside the iframe, and the embedded script/reload flow offers no fallback. The new spec even asserts failure 'with no referer', confirming this population is unhandled rather than accidental. This is a real correctness/availability defect introduced by this change.

judged_text: ensure_embeddable hard-fails on any request whose browser sends no Referer, with no fallback validation of the embed request. Visitors using privacy extensions, corporate proxies that strip Referer, or referrer-policy-suppressing setups get Discourse::InvalidAccess (a 403 error page) rendered inside the comment box on every view of every embedded article, with no way for the site owner to serve them; this client population is entirely unaddressed.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is denied unless `URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. When `request.referer` is nil/blank (e.g., Referrer stripped or `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`), `URI('')` yields a nil host, which fails the equality check and raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` ('invalid referer host'), rendering an error instead of the embed. The spec explicitly asserts this behavior (`it "raises an error with no referer"`). There is no alternative validation path using `params[:embed_url]` or similar fallback in this controller, so this client population cannot be served.
